chunks: And it was also narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about voluntary prayer during travel. He said: 'Do not pray anything before the two [rak'at] and after them during the day.'

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: The two [rak'at] (referring to the shortened obligatory prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on voluntary prayers during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'no nafl before or after' the obligatory travel prayer during daylight hours, reflecting the scholarly view that the two rak'ahs of safar serve as a complete unit of prayer in this context. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the travel prayer and other voluntary acts, ensuring that the traveler's worship remains concise and focused on the essential obligation.
